entities.name: PMID:25451388
observations: Denny et al. (2015), Journal of Affective Disorders, compared 17 avoidant personality disorder patients with 21 healthy controls during anticipation of and performance of cognitive reappraisal.
In avoidant personality disorder, amygdala hyper-reactivity during reappraisal anticipation was positively associated with increasing self-reported anxiety levels.

entities.name: Avoidant personality disorder
observations: The study assessed 17 patients and reported greater state and trait anxiety than healthy controls.
The study linked exaggerated amygdala activity during reappraisal anticipation with heightened anxiety in avoidant patients.

entities.name: Amygdala anticipation anxiety
observations: In a cross-sectional fMRI study of 17 avoidant personality disorder patients, greater amygdala reactivity during anticipation of cognitive reappraisal was positively associated with self-reported anxiety.

The authors noted that the signal may reflect anxiety about the upcoming reappraisal, the anticipated negative image, or scrutiny by experimenters; causal or longitudinal prediction was not established.
